entries.german:
Sitzung vom 12. Dezember 1569

[12. Dezember 1569] 12. Decembris VII. congregatio. Quidam chirurgi minister Stäntzl Schultess von Rosenberg in Masur, praesentatus loco prioris chirurgi ad magisterium sanitatis comparuit et examinatus est. Sed cum et juvenis esset et in chirurgicis administrationibus ita inexercitatus, ut illum omnia confundere, nec bubones aut anthraces curare posse, facile apparuerit, decrevit facultas, magistris balneatorum esse dicendum, facultatem mirari, cur ipsi tales homines chirurgiae imperitos ad examen praesentent, quos antea privatim de his rebus nec examinarint nec melius instruxerint. Quare facultatem nec hunc approbare posse, ut qui morbum non intelligat et praeter artis ignorantiam etiam linguae germanicae sit imperitus. Quod si non aptiorem ad hoc munus chirurgicum eligant, rem necessario ad consulem delatam iri. Proposui etiam facultati petitionem omnium balneatorum hujus urbis, scripto ad nos transmissam [fol. 142r] ut lit. F in actis ostendit, in qua significant, se hactenus ab excelso regimine non potuisse impetrare, ut balnea extra urbem in pagis ad duo milliaria clauderentur, cum interim plurimi subinde ex urbe et suburbiis eo lavatum exeant, atque in tam frequenti concursu hominum ex variis locis confluentium nova semper contagia contrahantur. Quare rogant ut et facultas medica per informationem scriptam hoc negotium sacro regimini indicet, declarato periculo, quod inde oritur. Conclusum est, decanum debere formam ejusmodi informationis ad regimen concipere et ad proximam congregationem, quae frequentior sit, facultati proponere.
entries.english:
Meeting of December 12, 1569

[December 12, 1569] 12. Decembris VII. congregatio. A certain surgical assistant Stäntzl, Sheriff of Rosenberg in Masuria, presented in place of the previous surgeon, appeared before the Faculty of Medicine for the medical master's examination and was examined. But since he was young and so inexperienced in surgical practices that it clearly appeared everything confused him, and he could not treat buboes or anthrax, the Faculty decreed that it should be said to the masters of bathhouses: the Faculty wonders why they present such men, ignorant of surgery, for examination, whom they had neither previously examined privately on these matters nor instructed more thoroughly. Therefore the Faculty cannot approve this one, since he does not understand diseases and, apart from ignorance of the art, is also unskilled in the German language. If they do not choose a more suitable person for this surgical office, the matter will necessarily be referred to the consul. I also presented to the Faculty the petition of all the bathhouse masters of this city, transmitted to us in writing [fol. 142r] as letter F shows in the records, in which they signify that hitherto they have not been able to obtain from the supreme government that baths outside the city in the villages within two miles be closed, since meanwhile many frequently go there to bathe from the city and suburbs, and in such frequent gathering of people converging from various places new contagia are always contracted. Therefore they request that the medical faculty also indicate this matter to the sacred government through a written report, declaring the danger that arises from it. It was concluded that the dean must draft such a report for the government and present it to the Faculty at the next congregation, which will be more heavily attended.
